story: In the spirituality of a Plains Native American people, there is a term for the sacred or the divine, usually translated as "Great Spirit" and occasionally as "Great Mystery." This concept is understood as the power or sacredness that resides in everything, resembling animistic and pantheistic beliefs. Every creature and object is described as holy, or as having aspects that are holy. Part of the term corresponds to the meaning "Great" or "large." Before contact with European Christian missionaries, the people used this term to refer to an organization or group of sacred entities whose ways were mysterious, thus giving rise to the translation "The Great Mystery." In more recent times, a Native American activist promoted the translation "Great Mystery" and argued that the spirituality of his people was not monotheistic, but rather centered on this broader, mysterious sacred power. Related terms for this same sacred concept, or a closely related one, exist in the languages of several neighboring peoples who speak languages related to that of the original people, showing that the idea of a great sacred power or mystery was shared, in some form, among a number of connected groups.
